**Finding submitted — deviation (T4C, high severity).**

- **What the document does:** Section 9 contains only cause-based (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and security/service-level (9.3) termination rights; Sections 6.2, 19.4 and 27.3 add narrow remedy-based exits. There is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and Section 2.1 expressly locks Customer into a USD 2,000,000/year, three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (term confirmed as three years by Section 8.1).
- **Why it fails:** With a term longer than 12 months and no Customer convenience right at all, the clause falls short of both the preferred and the fallback positions (which at minimum contemplate 60–90 days' notice with a capped exit fee). Vendor holds no convenience right, so nothing needed deleting on their side.
- **Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level):** new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, plus a minimal conforming edit to Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not negate it. The comment offers 60–90 days' notice as a fallback.
